behavior_class_name: Backdoor Persistence Service Foothold Behavior Class
description: Creates persistence by launching schtasks.exe via CreateProcessW to register a Windows Scheduled Task that executes when a user logs on. The task runs under the SYSTEM account and launches a benign marker payload that writes recurring log entries to confirm logon-triggered persistence behavior.

persistence_installer.role: launches schtasks.exe with an ONLOGON trigger configuration to create a SYSTEM-context scheduled task for the marker payload

marker_payload.role: benign executable launched by the scheduled task during user logon to log execution and confirm persistence behavior

registry: scheduled task registered in Task Scheduler subsystem
process: Task Scheduler launches A06_3d_SampleApp.exe during user logon
payload remains active in a continuous logging loop
file_system: log file grows over time with repeated 5-second beacon entries
host: Task visible in Task Scheduler GUI
Task Scheduler Operational logs may record task registration and launch
Sysmon Event ID 1 may capture schtasks.exe execution
Sysmon Event ID 1 may capture payload execution after logon
network: no HTTP or HTTPS traffic is required
no TCP command channel is opened

code_placement: Scheduled task registration logic is implemented in the installer by invoking schtasks.exe through CreateProcessW. Persistent execution confirmation is implemented in the marker payload through timestamped file logging.
execution_trigger: The installer executes manually. The persistence payload executes automatically whenever a user logon event satisfies the scheduled task trigger.
execution_target: Task Scheduler logon-trigger subsystem and marker executable at C:\Users\Public\A06_3d_SampleApp.exe
semantic_meaning: Demonstrates logon-triggered persistence using the Windows Task Scheduler command-line utility, where execution is tied to user authentication events and persists across reboots or logoff/logon cycles.

mitre_attack_mapping.note: Logon-triggered scheduled task persistence using schtasks.exe and SYSTEM execution context.

control_notes.payload_effect: writes recurring log entries confirming scheduled execution after user logon

success_conditions: installer successfully launches schtasks.exe through CreateProcessW
task is configured with an ONLOGON trigger
task is configured to run as SYSTEM
user logs off and logs back into the Windows analysis VM
Task Scheduler activates the logon trigger
payload writes an initialization log entry
payload continues writing beacon log entries every 5 seconds
log file grows over time with repeated entries
no network activity or secondary payload execution occurs
